questions.q: According to this lesson, what does a dbt Cloud environment actually configure?
options: A warehouse connection, a schema pattern, the dbt version, and optionally a locked Git branch
Only the color scheme of the dbt Cloud UI
Nothing — environments are purely cosmetic labels
A single, universal setting that applies to every dbt Cloud project at once
questions.explain: An environment bundles the connection, schema pattern, dbt version, and optionally a branch lock — a real, functional bundle of settings.

questions.q: What are the real, selectable deployment types shown in dbt Cloud's environment settings, according to the screenshot in this lesson?
options: General, Staging (STG), and Production (PROD)
Alpha, Beta, and Gamma
Only 'Production' exists as an option
Red, Yellow, and Green
questions.explain: The real dbt Cloud UI shows General, Staging (STG), and Production (PROD) as the deployment type options.

questions.q: Who gets a Development environment in dbt Cloud, per this lesson?
options: Every individual developer gets their own, scoped to their branch
Only the project's original creator ever gets one
Development environments are shared by the entire team as a single environment
Development environments don't exist in dbt Cloud
questions.explain: Development is personal and per-developer, scoped to that developer's branch — this connects back to Lesson 32's branch-per-developer schema isolation.

questions.q: Which environment should scheduled production jobs (from Lesson 34) be configured to run in?
options: Production — the environment real dashboards actually query
Development — so engineers can watch it live
It doesn't matter which environment a scheduled job runs in
Staging only, and never Production
questions.explain: Production is the environment intended for scheduled jobs and merged, tested code — the tables dashboards actually query.

questions.q: Tracing one pull request through this chapter's concepts, in what order does it touch environments, per this lesson?
options: Developed in Development, tested by Slim CI against Production's state in a temp/staging-like schema, then run for real in Production once merged
It skips Development entirely and starts in Production
It only ever touches the Staging environment and nothing else
Production is used first, then Development afterward
questions.explain: The lesson traces a PR from Development, through Slim CI's deferred comparison against Production in a temp schema, to a final scheduled run in Production.
